requiredEnvVars.name: NODE_ENV
requiredEnvVars.notes: Must be 'development', 'production', or 'test'. Determines app behavior and which validations run.

requiredEnvVars.name: PORT
requiredEnvVars.notes: Server port. Defaults to 5000 if not set, but validation fails if missing. Try 9090 for dev.

requiredEnvVars.name: DATABASE_URL
requiredEnvVars.notes: PostgreSQL connection string. Format: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname?schema=public. Connects to Postgres pool with 30-connection max, 5s timeout, 15s statement timeout.

requiredEnvVars.name: JWT_SECRET
requiredEnvVars.notes: Minimum 32 chars. Signs access tokens. Failed validation hard-stops boot with clear error message.

requiredEnvVars.name: JWT_REFRESH_SECRET
requiredEnvVars.notes: Signs refresh tokens. Minimum 32 chars. Same validation as JWT_SECRET.

requiredEnvVars.name: ENCRYPTION_KEY
requiredEnvVars.notes: Must be exactly 64-character hexadecimal string (32 bytes AES-256-GCM). Generated via: node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))". Boot validation includes format check—wrong length/encoding throws immediate error, preventing deep failures in OAuth callbacks.

requiredEnvVars.name: REDIS_URL
requiredEnvVars.notes: Optional. If set (or REDIS_HOST is set), enables embedding worker, email worker, AI coach call worker. Workers are lazy-imported; failures log warn but don't crash boot. Set to redis://localhost:6379 for local dev with background jobs.

requiredEnvVars.name: REDIS_HOST
requiredEnvVars.notes: Alternative to REDIS_URL. Defaults to 'localhost'. Parsed with REDIS_PORT (default 6379), REDIS_PASSWORD (optional).

requiredEnvVars.name: SMTP_HOST
requiredEnvVars.notes: Email server (registration OTP, password reset, etc.). Without it, registration OTP emails fail silently in test mode but throw serviceUnavailable in production.

requiredEnvVars.name: SMTP_PORT
requiredEnvVars.notes: Default 587. Set to 465 or SMTP_SECURE=true for TLS. Parsed as integer.

requiredEnvVars.name: SMTP_USER
requiredEnvVars.notes: SMTP auth username. Fallback to SMTP_FROM if not set.

requiredEnvVars.name: SMTP_PASS
requiredEnvVars.notes: SMTP auth password (plaintext in .env, never committed).

requiredEnvVars.name: SMTP_FROM
requiredEnvVars.notes: From address for emails. Defaults to noreply@balencia.com. Also used as SMTP_USER fallback.

requiredEnvVars.name: GEMINI_API_KEY
requiredEnvVars.notes: Google Gemini API key (primary LLM). If absent, /ai-coach/status returns available=false. Per-request errors, no boot failure.

requiredEnvVars.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
requiredEnvVars.notes: OpenAI API key (fallback LLM + embeddings). If both GEMINI and OPENAI keys absent, AI Coach disabled. Per-request errors, no boot failure.

requiredEnvVars.name: CORS_ORIGIN
requiredEnvVars.notes: Comma-separated list. Defaults to http://localhost:3000. Parsed and set on Express CORS middleware.

requiredEnvVars.name: LOG_LEVEL
requiredEnvVars.notes: debug, info, warn, error. Default 'info'. 'debug' emits every DB query line.

requiredEnvVars.name: ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS
requiredEnvVars.notes: true/false. Default true. Disables all cron jobs except crisis-follow-up and WhatsApp fleet (which have independent kill-switches). Useful for frontend-only dev.

requiredEnvVars.name: ENABLE_CRISIS_FOLLOWUP
requiredEnvVars.notes: true/false. Default true. Independent kill-switch for crisis 24h check-in job (exempt from ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS master switch).

requiredEnvVars.name: ENABLE_BAILEYS_FLEET
requiredEnvVars.notes: true/false. Default false. Enables WhatsApp Baileys fleet (session-based transport). Independent of ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS.

requiredEnvVars.name: ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS
requiredEnvVars.notes: Set to 'false' for frontend dev (disables all scheduled jobs except crisis-follow-up). Default 'true'.

serverBoot.bootSequence:
1. Load .env via dotenv.config() (src/index.ts line 6)
2. Validate required env vars (NODE_ENV, PORT, DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY). Fail hard if missing. ENCRYPTION_KEY format validated: must be 64-char hex (src/config/env.config.ts line 44).
3. Connect to PostgreSQL (src/index.ts line 154). On connect: set timezone=UTC, statement_timeout per env. Pool health checked via SELECT NOW(). Retry: max 5 attempts, exponential backoff. Fail hard if all attempts fail.
4. Verify 'roles' table exists (src/index.ts line 157). If missing, log error suggesting npm run db:migrate.
5. Create HTTP server and Socket.IO initialization (src/index.ts line 163-166).
6. If REDIS_URL or REDIS_HOST set (env.redis.enabled):
   - Lazy-import and start embedding worker (src/index.ts line 171). Fail: log warn, continue (graceful degradation).
   - Lazy-import and start email worker (src/index.ts line 184). Fail: log warn, continue.
   - Lazy-import and start AI coach call worker (src/index.ts line 194). Fail: log warn, continue.
7. If Redis NOT configured, log info 'Embedding/email workers skipped (Redis not configured...)'.
8. If documents feature enabled AND (cluster.worker not defined OR cluster.worker.id === 1): recover stuck documents (best-effort, never blocks boot).
9. HTTP server listen() on env.port/env.host (src/index.ts line 225). On listen:
   - Log server start (port, host, environment, pid, Node version).
   - If development, log API URLs.
   - Warn if entitlement.mode === 'shadow' in production.
10. Start background jobs (only if isSchedulerWorker AND ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS !== 'false'):
    - Register ~40+ cron jobs via schedulerRegistry (reminder-processor, daily-scoring, weekly-report, etc.) with staggered start times (90ms–3120ms after listen).
    - If ENABLE_CRISIS_FOLLOWUP !== 'false', register crisis-follow-up job (exempt from master ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS).
    - If WhatsApp enabled (ENABLE_BAILEYS_FLEET=true or WA_CLOUD_API_TOKEN set):
      - Register WhatsApp jobs (outbox-relay, proactive, behavior-baseline, automation-scheduler, fleet-reaper).
      - Call initWhatsAppLayer() (idempotent).
    - If !ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS, log 'Background jobs DISABLED' and log WhatsApp fleet decoupling if applicable.
11. If !backgroundJobsEnabled BUT WhatsApp fleet enabled: call initWhatsAppLayer() directly (start() guards double-start).
12. If !backgroundJobsEnabled BUT crisis-follow-up enabled: start crisisFollowUpJob directly.
13. Start activity event processor on all workers (src/index.ts line 392).
14. Attach graceful shutdown handlers (SIGTERM, SIGINT) → stop schedulers → close workers → disconnect DB → exit.

HARD FAIL scenarios (exit 1):
- Missing required env var (step 2).
- ENCRYPTION_KEY malformed (step 2).
- Database connection fails after 5 retries (step 3).
- HTTP listen() fails (EACCES on port, EADDRINUSE) (step 9).

GRACEFUL DEGRADATION scenarios (log warn, continue):
- Redis unavailable → workers not started, continue without caching/background-job queue.
- Embedding worker fails → skip embeddings, fall back to text-only search.
- Email worker fails → skip background email delivery (per-request email still works via SMTP).
- AI coach call worker fails → skip background AI coach calls, continue with sync chat.
- Stuck document recovery fails → log warn, continue (best-effort on next startup).
- WhatsApp layer init fails → log error, continue (no WhatsApp, but app runs).

Feature kill-switches (independent of ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS):
- ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=false → disable all scheduled jobs EXCEPT crisis-follow-up and WhatsApp fleet.
- ENABLE_CRISIS_FOLLOWUP=false → disable crisis follow-up job (safety path exempt even when ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=false).
- ENABLE_BAILEYS_FLEET=false → disable WhatsApp Baileys fleet (but Cloud API can still run if WA_CLOUD_API_TOKEN set).

serverBoot.aiProvider:
Provider selection: checks GEMINI_API_KEY (primary) and OPENAI_API_KEY (fallback).

**If both GEMINI_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are absent or fake:**
- GET /api/ai-coach/status returns { available: false, message: 'AI Coach is not configured. Please set OPENAI_API_KEY.' } (src/controllers/ai-coach.controller.ts line 83-91).
- POST /api/ai-coach/start, /message, /complete: returns 400 or 500 depending on where the missing key is detected (e.g., OpenAI client init fails, returns error to caller).
- No hard boot failure. The app starts normally; AI Coach routes just fail per-request with a clear error (e.g., "API key not found").
- Fallback: some routes return a fallback greeting if provider is unavailable (src/services/ai-coach/conversation/conversation.service.ts line 77-93).

**Hard vs soft failure:**
- Hard fail at boot: NONE for missing GEMINI/OPENAI keys.
- Per-request error: OpenAI or Gemini API call fails → throws ApiError (400/500) → middleware catches → JSON error response to client.
- Graceful fallback: if LLM is down, some endpoints return a static fallback message (no LLM call, no error thrown).

**Provider selection code (source of truth):**
- src/config/env.config.ts line 185-226: env.gemini and env.openai config objects.
- src/services/ai-coach/core/ai-provider.ts line 7-37: AIProvider constructor checks this.geminiApiKey and this.visionClient (OpenAI). isAvailable() returns true if either is set (line 35-36).
- src/controllers/ai-coach.controller.ts line 34-36: routerLlmClient = new OpenAI({apiKey: env.openai.apiKey}) if apiKey exists, else null. routerLlm() function (line 38-54) returns '' on any error, no throw.
- src/services/ai-coach/conversation/conversation.service.ts line 44-125: generateOpeningMessage() tries LangGraph greeting → falls back to static greeting if LLM fails. No exception thrown; graceful degradation.
serverBoot.otpEmail:
**Registration flow (requires OTP + email verification):**
1. POST /api/auth/register (src/controllers/auth/auth-registration.controller.ts line 43-98):
   - Client sends { email, firstName, lastName, password, dateOfBirth, gender }.
   - Server generates 4-digit OTP via createActivationToken() (line 70-71).
   - Sends OTP email via mailHelper.sendRegistrationOTPEmail() (line 74).
   - Returns { activationToken, message: 'Verification code sent to your email' }.
   - Email not verified at this stage.

2. POST /api/auth/verify-registration (line 105-150+):
   - Client sends { activationToken, activationCode }.
   - Server verifies JWT token (line 113-116).
   - Verifies 4-digit code matches (line 124-125).
   - If valid, creates user in DB with is_email_verified=true (line 139).
   - Auth complete; returns access + refresh tokens + user profile.

**Email requirement:**
- Login does NOT require email verification; only registration does.
- Registration OTP sent via SMTP (env.smtp config required).
- If SMTP not configured: email send fails → in test mode (NODE_ENV=test) silently continues, in production throws serviceUnavailable (line 81-86).

**Dev bypass:**
- NO code-level bypass for OTP requirement during registration.
- Workaround: use seed-test-users.ts to pre-create users with is_email_verified=true (line 49), avoiding SMTP.
- Or: seed a user and manually set is_email_verified=true in the DB after account creation.
- No OTP-less registration endpoint.

**OTP details:**
- 4-digit code (line 70).
- Token TTL: 10 minutes (hard-coded in mailHelper, line 78 'activation.ts').
- SMTP required: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, SMTP_FROM.
- No Twilio SMS fallback; email-only (Twilio config exists for WhatsApp, not for OTP).

**Local dev setup:**
- Option 1: Set SMTP_* env vars to a real email provider (SendGrid, Gmail, Mailgun).
- Option 2: Use MailHog / Ethereal (fake SMTP for testing); set SMTP_HOST=localhost:1025.
- Option 3: Use seed-test-users.ts to bypass registration entirely.
risks: ENCRYPTION_KEY validation is strict (64-char hex, 32 bytes). Typo or wrong length boots cleanly but then deep cryptography fails inside OAuth callbacks—the env.config validation (line 44-48) prevents this by checking at import time.

REDIS unavailable: all background jobs silently skipped (best-effort workers). Embedding, email, AI coach call workers logged as warn and continued. No user-facing error unless the client explicitly waits for a queued job.
Database pool: 30 max connections, 5s connect timeout, 15s statement timeout. Long-running migrations or queries time out—increase DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS if needed.
Missing GEMINI_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY: AI Coach returns empty/fallback responses per-request (no boot error). Client sees 'Coach is not configured' via /status endpoint.
SMTP not configured: registration OTP emails fail. In test mode, continues; in production, throws 503. Users cannot register.
ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=false: disables ~40 scheduled jobs (proactive messaging, daily-scoring, etc.), but crisis-follow-up and WhatsApp fleet run independently. This is intentional (safety paths).
JWT secrets (JWT_SECRET, JWT_REFRESH_SECRET) must be different in production. If both are the same, refresh-token attacks are possible (but validation passes).
Database must be PostgreSQL. Migrations assume pg driver. No automatic schema creation—npm run db:migrate must run before boot or roles table check will log error (not crash).
Socket.IO initialized on boot: if something hangs during socket setup, the server hangs before the listen() callback fires.
Cluster mode (CLUSTER_MODE=true in production): forking happens but workers all boot independently—make sure your scheduler registry or kill-switch logic doesn't run duplicate jobs on each worker.
WhatsApp session encryption (WA_SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY): falls back to ENCRYPTION_KEY if not set. If ENCRYPTION_KEY is weak, WhatsApp credentials are weakly encrypted at rest.
No explicit .env file validation for typos (e.g., 'DATBASE_URL' vs 'DATABASE_URL'). Missing var defaults silently, causing boot failures later (e.g., pool connect timeout).

authContracts.tokenPayload: IJwtPayload (src/types/index.ts:33-38) signed by generateTokens (src/middlewares/auth.middleware.ts:298-320): { userId, email, role, sessionId?, iat, exp } plus iss/aud set via jwt.sign options (not payload literal fields) - issuer=env.jwt.issuer (JWT_ISSUER, default 'balencia-api'), audience=env.jwt.audience (JWT_AUDIENCE, default 'balencia-client'). Access and refresh tokens share the same payload shape {userId,email,role} - only secret and TTL differ (access: JWT_SECRET/JWT_EXPIRES_IN; refresh: JWT_REFRESH_SECRET/JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN). sessionId is declared in the type but not populated by generateTokens as inspected.
authContracts.refreshFlow: POST /api/auth/refresh, guarded by verifyRefreshToken middleware (verifies against JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, issuer/audience) then the controller (auth-session.controller.ts:106-181) re-validates account isActive, compares the caller-supplied refresh token's SHA-256 hash against the single hash stored in users.refresh_token (one active refresh token per user - no multi-device session table found), and on success performs full rotation: mints a brand-new access+refresh pair via generateTokens and immediately overwrites users.refresh_token with the new hash, so the previous refresh token can never be reused (old-token replay after refresh returns 401 'Refresh token mismatch'). Logout (POST /api/auth/logout) nulls users.refresh_token, invalidating any outstanding refresh token immediately, but the short-lived access token is not revoked and stays valid until natural expiry (default 15m) since no denylist/JTI mechanism exists.
authContracts.notes: Env vars for TTL/secrets (src/config/env.config.ts:82-89): JWT_SECRET (required, has an unreachable-in-practice placeholder fallback), JWT_REFRESH_SECRET (same), JWT_EXPIRES_IN (default '15m'), JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN (default '7d'), JWT_ISSUER (default 'balencia-api'), JWT_AUDIENCE (default 'balencia-client'). API mount prefix: env.api.prefix = process.env.API_PREFIX || '/api' (env.config.ts:177), applied in src/app.ts:196 (`app.use(env.api.prefix, routes)`); auth router mounted at /auth under that (src/routes/index.ts:191) - effective paths are /api/auth/* unless API_PREFIX is overridden. Middlewares guarding authenticated routes: `authenticate` (auth.middleware.ts:125-144 - extracts Bearer header or access_token cookie, verifies JWT, re-loads user row from DB every request to check is_active and get live role) used on /me, /onboarding-status, /profile (PATCH), /logout, /change-password, /complete-profile, /consent, /whatsapp/*; `verifyRefreshToken` (auth.middleware.ts:265-293) guards only /refresh; `optionalAuth` and `authorize()`/`authorizeOwnerOrAdmin` exist for other route families but are not used on the /auth router itself. Rate limiting: authLimiter on register/verify-registration/social/login/refresh; strictLimiter on resend-registration-otp/forgot-password/reset-password/change-password/whatsapp-enroll; dedicated per-user 30-req/min limiter on GET /me. Error shape sent to clients for thrown ApiError instances via the global error handler (distinct from the also-present but apparently-unused-by-auth-controllers ApiResponse.error* static methods, which have a slightly different shape with no `code` field): `{ success:false, message, code, errors?: AppErrorDetails[], timestamp, stack? (dev only), requestId? }` with HTTP status = ApiError.statusCode (src/middlewares/error.middleware.ts:241-263). Presence-only secrets check: found .env.example at yhealth-app/server/.env.example; no .env file and no .local-secrets/ directory present in server root (values not read/reported, presence only).
risks: Google social-auth verification fallback: if oauthService.verifySocialToken() throws for ANY reason (including a genuinely forged/invalid idToken, not just network issues), auth-registration.controller.ts:340-345 catches it, logs a warning, and falls back to trusting the client-supplied email/providerId directly - a network hiccup and a forged token are handled identically, weakening the claimed security guarantee; confirm NextAuth's server-side verification is actually enforced upstream, otherwise this is a spoofable account-creation/takeover vector.

Access tokens are not revocable server-side (no denylist/JTI blacklist) - logout only invalidates the refresh token; a stolen/leaked access token remains valid for its full TTL (default 15 minutes) even after logout.

mobileState.authSession: SecureStore key: 'balencia.mobile.session.v1'. Stores AuthSession = {accessToken, refreshToken?, expiresIn?, user?: UserSummary, storedAt}. clientEvidence.notes: READ-ONLY INVENTORY — no .env/.p8 secrets. Auth token storage is critical for mobile port: SecureStore on iOS replaces HTTP-only cookies; same re-install flow applies. LCM (Life Correlation Matrix) is foundational: 10 domains with Bayesian-learned personal weights; single GET /v1/intelligence/lcm provides full effective matrix for life-areas UI. Idempotency keys required for: AI Coach messages, image analysis, workout AI generation, goal generation (all credit-consuming).
